title: Workplace safety charges laid in 2024 shooting death of Edmonton security guard
summary: Workplace safety charges have been laid in connection with the death of an Edmonton security guard who was shot on the job two years ago.

image.caption: Harshandeep Singh, 20, was shot and killed inside a central Edmonton apartment building in the early morning of Dec. 6, 2024, while he was working as a security guard. (Submitted by Navjot Singh Shergill)

blocks.text: Edmonton
Workplace safety charges have been laid in connection with the death of an Edmonton security guard who was shot on the job two years ago.
Harshandeep Singh was patrolling downtown apartment building alone and at night
Harshandeep Singh, 20, died on Dec. 6, 2024, after he was found unresponsive in a stairwell by police officers responding to a call about reported gunshots at a downtown Edmonton apartment building.
Singh, who had moved to Canada from India as an international business student, was patrolling the property alone at night. It was his third day on the job.

His employer, National Security Guard Protection Services Inc., was charged last week with failing to ensure his safety and failing to address the previous violence reported at the property, according to the provincial government's Occupational Health and Safety (OHS) website.
According to the OHS charges, Singh was conducting security patrols in the apartment building at 10603 107th Ave., when he was assaulted and then fatally shot.
The building had been the site of a previous shooting on Nov. 21, 2024, two weeks before Singh's death.
Two weeks after his death, the apartment building was shut down by the City of Edmonton over "serious safety concerns," triggering the relocation of more than 60 tenants.

items: Man shot 2 weeks earlier in same Edmonton building where security guard slain

blocks.text: National Security Guard Protection Services Inc. is facing a total of five charges under the Occupational Health and Safety Act, for failing to reassess the hazards at the work site in a timely manner “after violent incidents occurred” and for failing to withdraw security guard services from the building when the hazards could no longer be “eliminated or controlled.”
Investigators further allege the Alberta-based company failed to ensure the necessary hazard assessments and violence prevention plans were adopted, and revised as necessary.
The company has not responded to a request for comment on the charges.

blocks.text: Singh, a NorQuest College student, took the security job because he wanted to build experience for a career in policing.

His death triggered calls for better protections and improved safety standards for security guards, and prompted the Alberta government to announce plans to change its mandatory training programs for licensed security guards in the province.
Harshandeep Singh, 20, was killed in a 2024 shooting while working as a security guard in an Edmonton apartment building. Workplace safety charges have now been laid in his death. (Samuel Martin/CBC)
A man and woman have been charged in Singh’s killing.
Evan Chase Rain, 31, is facing a charge of first-degree murder. Judith Saulteaux, also 31, has had her charge downgraded to second-degree murder.
Record records show their trials are expected to get underway in late February 2027.
